newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay names CITIC Pacific's Fan deputy chairman.
newsitem.headline: Cathay names CITIC Pacific's Fan deputy chairman.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Tuesday that its board has approved the appointment of Henry Fan, managing director of CITIC Pacific Ltd, as deputy chairman of the airline effective January 1.
The non-executive position recognises the substantial relationship between the airline and CITIC Pacific, Cathay Pacific said.

"I am delighted that Henry has accepted this appointment, which I believe reflects the support and long-term nature of CITIC's relationship with the airline," Cathay Pacific chairman Peter Sutch said in a statement.
CITIC Pacific has a 25 percent interest in Cathay Pacific.
The two companies also hold stakes in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines, with CITIC Pacific having 28 percent and Cathay Pacific holding 18 percent.
Tuesday's announcement signals a further intertwining of the interests of the two companies.

Cathay and its parent Swire Pacific Ltd, one of Hong Kong's venerable trading houses, agreed in April to sell about 18 percent of of Dragonair out of their then 43 percent stake to state-owned China National Aviation Corp (CNAC).
CITIC Pacific also sold part of its Dragonair holdings the CNAC, giving the Chinese carrier a controlling 36 percent stake.

In a related deal, Cathay Pacific issued 573 million new shares to CITIC Pacific, lifting the conglomerate's stake in the airline from 10 percent to 25 percent while trimming Swire's holding to 44 percent from 53 percent.

Fan was in the news on Monday when CITIC Pacific announced a management team led by chairman Larry Yung would buy 330 million shares or 15.47 percent of the company for HK$33 per share, a substantial discount to the HK$44.90 at Tuesday's close.
Fan lifted his interest in CITIC Pacific, a unit of China International Trust & Investment Corp Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd, by 30 million shares or 1.41 percent, it said.
CITIC Hong Kong is the local investment arm of China's state-owned trading giant China International Trust & Investment Corp. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441
